LanguageData.LoadingProgress.PatchInitialization: Patch late-loading initialization code to show loading progress
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.PatchInitialization.Tip: When enabled, the mod will patch the part during RimWorld's startup process where the game typically hangs to make it more responsive. This allows the mod to track and display loading progress for each static constructor. This should not cause any problems unless you are running mods that very specifically have targeted this code and is very timing sensitive.\n\nIf you experience any issues with Loading Progress, try disabling this setting to see if it resolves the issue.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.PatchReloadContent: Patch content loading code to show loading progress
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.PatchReloadContent.Tip: When enabled, the mod will replace the method that loads mod content to track and display loading progress for each content pack being reloaded. This should not cause any problems unless you are running mods that very specifically have targeted this code. The mod will log a warning if it detects any other mods patching this code.\n\nIf you experience any issues with Loading Progress, try disabling this setting to see if it resolves the issue. Feel free to report any problems you encounter with mods that triggered the warning message.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.ShowInGameLoadingProgres: Show loading progress during in-game generation/loading
When enabled, the mod shows a loading window during in-game long operations too, such as generating a new world, generating the map for a new game, and loading a save.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.PatchInGameDeferredRepai: Patch in-game renderer regeneration to keep the loading window responsive

When enabled, the mod also makes the map/world renderer regeneration that happens after generating or loading finishes (part of the process that otherwise freezes the loading window for its whole duration) run in smaller pieces with repaints in between, so the window keeps updating instead of appearing to hang. This applies to new games, loaded saves, settling or generating maps in-play, and world generation.\n\nIf you experience any issues with Loading Progress, try disabling this setting to see if it resolves the issue.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.LastLoadingTime.Tip: When enabled, the mod will display the time elapsed so far. Once the game has loaded at least once, it will store it for next time, and use it as the estimated loading time for the next loading session.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.LoadingTimesCapacity.Tip:
How many previous load times to remember when calculating the estimated loading time.

The estimate is a weighted average that gives the 10 most recent launches progressively more influence (from 1× for the 10th-most-recent up to 10× for the most recent). Any launches beyond those 10 all receive equal weight (1×), so they are never completely ignored no matter how many you store.

A higher value produces a more stable estimate by smoothing out one-off slow or fast loads.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.ClearEstimatesOnModListC: Clear estimates when mod list changes

When enabled, the stored load time history is cleared whenever the mod list changes. This ensures that the estimate always reflects your current mod setup.\n\nDisable this if you want the estimate to persist across mod list changes, for example if you frequently add or remove mods and still want a rough baseline.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.LoadingTimeAsCountDown.T: When enabled, the mod will display the loading time as a countdown, starting from the estimated loading time. This is useful to see how much time is left until the game is fully loaded.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.LastLoadingTimeProgressB: When enabled, the mod will show a progress bar during loading that indicates how much time has passed since the game started loading compared to the expected time.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.LastLoadingTimeInCorner: Show loading time in bottom-right corner of the main menu
When enabled, the mod will show the time it took to load the game in the bottom-right corner of the main menu.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.ShowMemoryUsage.Tip: When enabled, the loading window shows the current managed (Mono) heap size and the game process's total memory usage (working set).\n\nThe process figure is the more useful one for judging overall RAM pressure; the heap figure is a narrower measure of only the .NET-managed portion of memory.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.ShowFasterGameLoadingEar: Show Faster Game Loading's early mod content loading progress
When enabled, and Faster Game Loading is active, the mod will show an additional loading indicator for mod content that is loaded early during the game startup process.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.TrackStartupLoadingImpac: When enabled, the mod will track the impact of startup loading impact from mods and the base game allowing you to see a detailed breakdown of what is causing the biggest delays during the loading process.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.AutoSaveStartupImpactRep: When enabled, the startup impact report is automatically saved to StartupImpactData.xml in your RimWorld save data folder after every game startup, without having to open the startup impact window and press Save.\n\nThis lets external tools, such as the RimSort mod manager, show each mod's startup load time.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.ShowBaseGameOffThreadImp: - Show base game's background-thread startup impact

When enabled, the startup impact window shows a second bar under the base game's impact bar, breaking down the time the base game spent doing work on background threads during startup, separately from its main thread work.\n\nThis is off by default because most people won't find it particularly informative, but it's here if you want the extra detail.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.ProgressBarColor.Tip: The color of the main progress bar in the loading progress window.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.SmallBarColor.Tip: The color of the sub-stage indicator on the main progress bar in the loading progress window.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.CustomPlacementPreview.T: Drag this window to where you want the loading window to appear, then close it. It can't be dragged off-screen, and its position is kept relative to your screen size, so it stays in the same relative spot if you change resolution.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.SessionsToKeep.Tip:
How many past startup impact sessions to keep on disk.

A session costs roughly 950 bytes per mod, so on a 230-mod list each one is around 220 KB. The oldest session drops off once the limit is reached.

This is separate from 'Estimates to store' above, which counts loading time samples feeding the estimate rather than sessions on disk.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.KeepPinnedSessions: - Keep pinned sessions past that limit
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.KeepPinnedSessions.Tip: When enabled, a pinned session is never the one dropped when the limit is reached, and does not occupy one of the slots.\n\nTurn this off to have pinned sessions age out like any other, with the pin affecting only where they appear in the list.
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.KeepUnfinishedBoots: - Keep sessions from startups that never finished
LanguageData.LoadingProgress.KeepUnfinishedBoots.Tip: A startup that hangs or crashes partway through writes no report at all today, which loses the runs with the most diagnostic value.\n\nWhen enabled, a small marker is kept while the game loads and removed once it finishes. One still present at the next startup becomes a history entry recording when that startup began and which loading stage it reached. There is no per-mod breakdown for such a run, because the game stopped before there was one.
